newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian opposition says not linked to bomb blasts.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian opposition says not linked to bomb blasts.

text.p: The umbrella NADECO opposition group said on Wednesday it was not involved in bomb explosions that have rocked Nigeria's biggest city Lagos and called for thorough investigations of the incidents to find the culprits.
"NADECO is not involved at all," Reverend Tunji Adebiyi, a spokesman for the National Democratic Coalition told Reuters.

Several local newspapers quoted NADECO's 88-year-old leader Michael Ajasin as saying from his home in Owo, southwestern Nigeria that rather than continuing to blame his group for the bombings the government should "look beyond NADECO to trace those who are really involved."
On Tuesday, the latest in recent bomb attacks on military targets tore apart a bus full of soldiers, killing two and wounding 29 including two civilians.
It was the third blast since December and although no one has claimed responsibility the authorities have blamed the opposition in the politically volatile nation.
Africa's most populous nation plunged into crisis in 1993 when the army annulled an election which was to restore democracy.
NADECO emerged as a coalition of pro-democracy, human rights and student movements to press for the results of the poll to be accepted.

It was the force behind wealthy businessman Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of the voided vote, who declared himself president in 1994 in defiance of the army and has since been detained along with many of his supporters.
Adebiyi said the military government should enter into dialogue with NADECO to resolve the political crisis.
"NADECO does not support violence. What we are looking for is reconciliation through genuine dialogue," he said.
